title: Classical Krawtchouk identification and native vanishing
statement: For the declared reference amplitude, n(A,R,delta,f) equals 2^(R-1)(-1)^A times the coefficient of y^(R-1-f) in (1+y)^(A+R-delta)(1-y)^(-A); at delta=2A+R it vanishes for odd d=R-1-f and has the stated binomial closed form for even d. The object is the MacWilliams-Sloane binary Krawtchouk polynomial at a negative argument and a possibly-negative length, n = 2^(R-1)(-1)^A K_d(-A; R-delta); orthogonality is not available at these parameters and is not relied on, while the generating function and the q=2 reflection law are.
verified: The isolated integer centralCoefficient cancellation theorem compiles under the pinned Lean 4.34.1 workbench and its proof boundary contains no sorry, admit, or added axiom.
A no-escape Lean counterexample proves the first entry_closed_form candidate false as stated; the native entry is 0 while its proposed right side is -1.
The guarded revision passed 134370 licensed binary comparisons and two deliberate mutant families.

Five source-bridge facts compile without proof escapes: orbit mismatch characterization and support, active-coordinate swap-state equality, exact integer signed-subword expansion, and native delta characterization.
Inactive selected coordinates make the native ordered difference vanish at every point in the source swap orbit.
The guarded binomial term is the exact cardinality of the fixed-size active subsets containing mismatches.erase t.

The corrected guarded entry_closed_form compiles against the pinned native LayoutNumerator.entry under the declared orbit and pivot-mismatch hypotheses, with no proof escapes in the copied source boundary.

The parity interpolant reflection law compiles in a separate no-escape Lean module by rational-polynomial interpolation uniqueness; the earlier admitted reflection step is no longer a mathematical blocker.

Hash-bound local Cycle 9 receipts report a fresh exact replay of the no-escape native centered-vanishing and A=0 collapse chain; the replay archive and complete newer source chain are not yet imported into this checkout.

The v0.1 public envelope binds the complete 41-module transitive OAI closure for the nine shared native targets, exact Lean and mathlib pins, and an executable logical-dependency ceiling.

The public replay driver recompiles the centered-vanishing, A=0 and parity-coefficient targets from a project with no pre-existing CBMD proof objects; its dedicated CI job performs the same pinned replay.

The identification is exact and reproducible in-repo: the amplitude equals 2^(R-1)(-1)^A K_d(-A; R-delta) on 6,048 classes with no mismatch, and the closed form equals the defining Newton construction on 2,352.

The binary reflection law K_m(n-x) = (-1)^m K_m(x) holds on 6,048 classes, and on the centred line the length is -2A and the argument is exactly n/2, so the odd-degree vanishing is that law's root fact; 128 vanishing odd degrees and 148 non-zero even degrees occur, so neither case is empty.
unresolved: an independent source-specific derivation and convention audit; the prior-art search settled the mathematics' provenance, not whether the reference amplitude is correctly read off the source conventions
nonclaims: not a novelty determination or external independent verification
orthogonality is not available at these parameters: the argument lies outside 0..n and the length may be negative, so the measure does not exist and the earlier phrasing claiming it is withdrawn
the Krawtchouk identification is a naming observation, not a theorem; writing C(-A, j) with the generalized binomial turns the Krawtchouk sum into this dossier's own convolution

the centered vanishing is a published root fact about binary Krawtchouk polynomials (Coleman 2011), and the coefficient-extraction form is Newton interpolation with Vandermonde convolution; neither is claimed as new
smallest_decisive_test: Independently rederive the source-specific coefficient identity or identify the first hypothesis or coordinate convention at which the bundled native correspondence fails.
